Observation of a male and two females after searching for long minutes for the origin of unidentified calls. Perched above me and visibly very disturbed by my presence, the male was the least mobile and perched lowest (about 5m). He tried several times to intimidate me by bristling his hair and shaking a branch  with his 4 limbs while emitting 3 warning calls, sometimes accompanied by grunts. The females, perched higher up, were the most nervous and constantly moved from one branch to another while never taking their eyes off me. These are the ones uttering very high-pitched "clacking" calls. The scene lasted for several minutes after which I moved away (I had disturbed them enough as it was).

I always hear the exact same sound; the volume varies, but it consistently seems to come from that same location.

I did previously have a single mouse in my house, but an exterminator inspected the entire property, including the attic, and found nothing unusual. I even mentioned this sound to him, and he checked the attic right above that specific spot but didn't notice anything.

I live in remote ranch country in Deep South Texas, about 60 miles north of the USA/Mexican border. I clearly heard the sound from inside. I went outside to investigate and my two dogs were standing still and quiet, staring intently in the direction of the sound, which was to the west. I brought them inside and returned outside, all the while listening to the sound. I turned on the audio recording application in my iPhone and recorded 30 seconds of the sound. I walked toward the location from where the sound came but it stopped and never repeated the rest of the evening. I do not believe it was a bird, but a medium-sized mammal, perhaps a fox, bobcat, or mountain lion, all of which are known to this area.

The recording is not altered in any way. The wind was blowing steadily because a rainstorm was approaching. The vegetation is Texas thorn-scrub brush with mostly mesquite trees but some Texas ebony and huisache trees as well. The area has been in severe drought so there was just a little bit of live grass in the understory.
